insurance.name: Hull Coverage
insurance.description: Covers insured vessel damage subject to maintenance, operating-area and crew qualification requirements.
insurance.frontier_note: Rates rise sharply beyond routine rescue coverage.

insurance.name: Cargo Coverage
insurance.description: Protects cargo owner against loss or damage; handling requirements become contractual obligations.

insurance.name: Carrier Liability
insurance.description: Covers damage caused by vessel operations, cargo handling or docking incidents.

insurance.name: Salvage and Recovery Rider
insurance.description: Pays defined recovery costs rather than leaving a captain to negotiate from distress.

insurance.name: Expedition Coverage
insurance.description: Specialized coverage for survey work; may require filed route, reserve margins and certified environmental equipment.

credit_practices: Independent captains often finance ships over many years; the lender may effectively own the vessel until final payment.
A ship with excellent maintenance records can be worth substantially more than an identical neglected hull.
Frontier contracts may offer fuel advances or guaranteed backhaul rather than simply higher rates.
Large carriers negotiate fuel and docking contracts unavailable to independents; independents compensate by taking irregular freight.
A catastrophic repair can turn a profitable captain into an employee or force sale of the ship without anyone behaving villainously.

common_terms.meaning: No lender, salvage claimant or other recorded party has an ownership interest in the ship.
Derogatory term for a vessel technically worth less than the debt secured against it.
Used-ship description indicating documented required work is current; not a claim that the ship is cosmetically clean.
Insurance clause denying or limiting coverage beyond named supported systems.

insurance_design.summary: Insurance is normally voluntary, but lenders, ports, cargo owners, passenger contracts and hazardous facilities may require certificates as a condition of doing business.
insurance_design.policy_violation: Captains can operate outside policy restrictions. Violations may remain undiscovered, be detected through records, or surface during a claim; consequences can include cancellation, nonrenewal, higher premiums or denial of a materially related claim.
insurance_design.registration_relationship: Insurers generally expect a recognized current vessel registration and may suspend or restrict coverage after major undocumented configuration changes.
